recipes.name: Mushroom-Smothered Beef Burgers
ingredients_raw: 1 (10.75 ounce) can Campbell's® Condensed Cream of Mushroom Soup (Regular or 98% Fat Free)

steps.text: Thoroughly mix 1/4 cup soup, beef, bread crumbs, onion and egg in a large bowl. Shape the beef mixture firmly into 4 (1/2-inch-thick) burgers.
Heat the oil in a 10-inch skillet over medium-high heat. Add the burgers and cook until they're well browned on both sides. Pour off any fat.
Add the remaining soup, Worcestershire, water and mushrooms to the skillet and heat to a boil. Reduce the heat to low. Cover and cook for 10 minutes or until the burgers are cooked through.

raw_recipe.headline: Mushroom-Smothered Beef Burgers
raw_recipe.description: There's nothing more satisfying and delicious than these tasty, quick-cooking, beef burgers served with a creamy mushroom gravy.

review.reviewBody: My husband really enjoyed this. I used a really lean ground beef and also added a clove of minced garlic, served with mashed potatoes...it's very comforting!

Delicious comfort food! I am sensitive to gluten so had to make a few small changes. Used homemade soup from a recipe on this site and omitted the bread crumbs and Worcestershire sauce. I added garlic powder instead of onions (don't like them) and some pepper. I didn't need the water since my soup wasn't condensed. After cooking with the lid on, I cooked an additional 10 min with the lid off to thicken the soup sauce. Served over quinoa, tasted great! Next time will add more soup over top to make more sauce.
Great flavor! Suggestions: I doubled the Worcestershire, and added minced garlic. I would remove the patties after step 2, then add them back to skillet after mixing everything together, then simmer.

I enjoyed this recipe. i used ground venison because I had some in the freezer. I used Slap Ya Mama Seasoning in the burger and gravy. i am glad I doubled the gravy as one of the other reviewers did. i will definitely make this again.

This was a big hit. Needed more salt and more Worcestershire sauce, in my opinion, and a bit more water to make more sauce. I also put in more fresh mushrooms. This is NOT a criticism of the original recipe! I like a recipe that can be easily adjusted to suit different tastes.

yummy, easy comfort food. I made mine even easier when I found pre-formed turkey burger patties on sale. The pre-formed patties, one can of soup, a bit of water, a can of mushrooms, and a splash of worcestershire and dinner was ready in less than 20 minutes. (I served with rice and steamed veggies)

DH & I were both sick and wanted something comforting, yet not too troublesome to make. I didn't add to the meat, simply browning up well seasoned burgers, then removed from pan, sauteed the onions and some mini-Bella mushrooms, added the soup, more water than called for, and the Worcestershire sauce and then returned meat to pan and simmered as directed. Served with mashed potatoes and greenbeans and while not visually appealing, it certainly hit the spot. Will likely make again.
Really good! I didn't have mushroom soup so I used Cream of Chicken. My husband and I really enjoyed this and he has asked me to make it again. Thanks Campbell's!

Great recipe. My husband loved this. I only had Golden Mushroom soup so that is what I used. I substituted minced dried onion for the fresh (2 Tbl worth). This really needed a lot more gravy though and it barely covered the burger patties. I will definitely make this again with the Golden Mushroom soup and double the sauce part. I left out the extra mushrooms since the soup had plenty.
A very nice and easy patty. I simmered it for an extra 10 minutes and served it over whole wheat pasta. I will definitely be adding it to my recipe box. Thanks for the recipe.

This is good. I have been making a very similar dish for awhile. The only difference is that I don't add the worcestershire sauce or the water to the final sauce. It is good both ways. This version has a stronger tasting sauce because of the worcestershir, but they are both good.

This is a very good recipe. Be sure to use 90% lean beef or learner and they won't fall apart as easily. I also recommend using more than one can of cream of mushroom soup and double the worcestershire sauce.
This tastes delicious, but my patties fell apart. They seemed too wet. I think next time I will reduce the amount of soup and onions.
Very good as is
This was amazing! The flavor was hearty. Came out really moist. Burgers fell apart instantly when served, though. I might try very lean ground beef next time I make this.
My kids and friends loved it . Really juicy and soft. Full of flavours
I made this according to the recipe and it was delicious.
It's a good recipe only problem i had that it didn't hold it shape.. other than that i will make it again.
Our burgers fell apart! I am thinking we used too many onions. It had great taste though. May try again sometime.
served with egg noodles. my whole family loved these!
